content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} state sales tax on a vehicle, plus a county rate, a small title fee and a small registration fee. A yearly vehicle license tax based on the vehicle's list price is the largest ongoing cost.

howItWorks.text: The state rate is {stateRate}. A trade-in lowers the price the tax is figured on. Counties add their own rate, and cities charge a separate tax that varies by city.
If you buy from a dealer in another state and register the vehicle here, you owe use tax at the same state rate. The state reduces it by the tax you already paid in the other state.
The vehicle license tax is charged when you register and again each year. It is figured from the vehicle's original list price and gets smaller as the vehicle ages.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in Arizona?
faq.text: Yes. The state taxes the sales price less the value of the vehicle traded in.

faq.q: What if I buy a car in another state?
faq.text: Arizona charges use tax when you register it here, and reduces it by the sales tax you paid elsewhere. Enter that amount in the calculator.

faq.q: Why is the vehicle license tax not in the total?
faq.text: It depends on the vehicle's original list price and age, which the calculator does not ask for, so it is shown as not included.
No. Cities charge their own tax on vehicle sales and rates differ by city, so it is shown as not included.
